name: SideProjects

sources.title: Homepage — daily launchpad for indie makers, 'Submit your project — it's free'
Pricing — Free queue launch, $29 Skip-the-line, $15 Relaunch, $8/mo Pro, sponsor options
Submit project — requires account; unauthenticated visitors get a login/register wall

conditions: Free launch requires a registered account (email + password at /register)
Free launches go into a queue and go live 'when a slot opens, usually within a few weeks' — no date control
Only paid Skip-the-line ($29) lets you pick an exact launch date and guarantees newsletter inclusion
requirements: A real side project / indie product to launch
Account registration is mandatory before the submit form is reachable
Project is placed into a daily launch list; top 3 by unique reactions win a badge at midnight
preparation: Category selection (AI, Developer tools, Productivity, Design, Marketing, Writing, Health, Audio, Community, Games, etc.)
Decide free queue vs $29 Skip-the-line vs $15 Relaunch for an existing project
workflow: Fill the project submission form (name, URL, tagline, categories)
Free route: join the queue and wait for an open launch slot
Paid route: pick a date via Skip-the-line ($29, Stripe checkout)
On launch day the project appears in 'Launching today' and collects emoji reactions/comments; top 3 win a badge
watchFor: Submit URL redirects unauthenticated users to /login — account creation is unavoidable
Free tier explicitly warns of multi-week queue time; Do not promise a launch date on the free plan
Upsells at checkout-adjacent pages: $99/week featured spot, $150 newsletter sponsor, $120 written review
Relaunch ($15) only applies to a project already launched once
Reactions count for the daily top-3 badge; engagement on launch day affects visibility
countsAsLive: Project appears on the homepage 'Launching today' list on its launch day and has a permanent /projects/<slug> page accepting reactions and comments
unknowns: Exact queue length / wait time for free launches beyond 'a few weeks'
Whether submissions can be rejected and on what grounds
What fields beyond name/URL/tagline/categories the logged-in submit form contains
